pointers.sentence: 6.1 came out on 5 August 2026, the day after 5.2.17 and 6.0.8 (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`), with a patch of its own for each fix of that day (`docs/releases/security.txt`).
6.1 came out on 5 August 2026, the day after 5.2.17 and 6.0.8 (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`), with a patch of its own for each fix of that day (`docs/releases/security.txt`).

`SessionMiddleware.process_response` now adds `"Cookie"` to `"Vary"` whenever it sets or deletes the cookie, and when the session was read (`django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py:SessionMiddleware.process_response`; [`SessionMiddleware`: the cookie and the save](../auth/session-middleware.md)).

A `"Vary"` of `"*"` used to be stored (CVE-2026-6907; 5.2.14, 6.0.5), as did a star with white space around it (CVE-2026-48587; 5.2.15, 6.0.6); `has_vary_header` now compares stripped names (`django/utils/cache.py:has_vary_header`).
`UpdateCacheMiddleware.process_response`, which `cache_page` runs too, returns a response unstored at the first check that holds (`django/middleware/cache.py:UpdateCacheMiddleware.process_response`).

Since it writes a header into `HttpRequest.META` as WSGI does, its hyphens as underscores, a header named x_forwarded_for landed on X-Forwarded-For's key, past a proxy that strips X-Forwarded-For (`django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIRequest.__init__`; [Making the request: `WSGIRequest` and `ASGIRequest`](../http/request.md#from-an-asgi-scope)).

Its pattern ends at `"\Z"`, where `"$"` would match before a final newline (`django/core/validators.py:DomainNameValidator.__init__`; [Validators: `django/core/validators.py`](../forms/validators.md)).

Its pattern ends at `"\Z"`, where `"$"` would match before a final newline (`django/core/validators.py:DomainNameValidator.__init__`; [Validators: `django/core/validators.py`](../forms/validators.md)).
A newline let through could inject a header into a response, though `HttpResponse` refuses one in a header (`django/http/response.py:ResponseHeaders._convert_to_charset`).
At this commit `log_response` leaves the escaping to `log_message` (`django/utils/log.py:log_message`; [Logging](../startup/logging.md)).

Since then `WSGIRequestHandler.log_message` hands its arguments to `log_message`, and no 6.0 note says so (`django/core/servers/basehttp.py:WSGIRequestHandler.log_message`; [The development server](../commands/runserver.md)).

`verify_password` now hashes random characters when the stored password is unusable or its hasher unknown, or the password given is `None` (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:verify_password`; [Authenticating: `authenticate` and the backends](../auth/authenticating.md)).

At this commit it calls `check_password_with_timing_attack_mitigation`, which hashes for nothing when there is no user (`django/contrib/auth/handlers/modwsgi.py:check_password`, `django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:check_password_with_timing_attack_mitigation`).

At this commit it calls `check_password_with_timing_attack_mitigation`, which hashes for nothing when there is no user (`django/contrib/auth/handlers/modwsgi.py:check_password`, `django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:check_password_with_timing_attack_mitigation`).

`PasswordResetForm.send_mail` now logs the failure to `"django.contrib.auth"` (`django/contrib/auth/forms.py:PasswordResetForm.send_mail`; [Password reset: `PasswordResetTokenGenerator` and the reset views](../auth/password-reset.md)).

It refuses an absolute name or one with `".."` among its parts (`django/core/files/storage/base.py:Storage.save`; [File storage: `Storage`, `FileSystemStorage` and `storages`](../services/storage.md)).

`extract`, which startproject and startapp use for a template archive, refuses a member unless `os.path.commonpath` of its path and the target is the target (`django/utils/archive.py:BaseArchive.target_filename`; [Paths and archives: `safe_join`, `safe_makedirs` and `extract`](../utils/paths.md)).

`FileSystemStorage`, given a mode for directories, and `FileBasedCache` make their directories through `safe_makedirs` and so `makedirs`, which sets each mode with `os.chmod` after `os.mkdir` (`django/utils/_os.py:makedirs`).

`GenericInlineModelAdmin.get_formset` gives its forms a `BaseForm.has_changed` that answers false for a new row the user may not add, or an existing one they may not change, as `InlineModelAdmin.get_formset` does (CVE-2026-4277; 5.2.13, 6.0.4; `django/contrib/contenttypes/admin.py:GenericInlineModelAdmin.get_formset`; [Inlines: `InlineModelAdmin` and its formsets](../admin/inlines.md)).

`ModelAdmin._save_formset` raises `BadRequest` for a changed form whose object is new (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin._save_formset`; [The change list's columns: `list_display` and `list_editable`](../admin/list-display.md)).
`display_for_field` makes a model's URL field a link only if `URLValidator` accepts the value, whatever the field's own validators allow (`django/contrib/admin/utils.py:display_for_field`).
The salt now carries a prefix and the given salt's length (`django/core/signing.py:_cookie_signer_salt`).

The old salt is still read while the setting `SIGNED_COOKIE_LEGACY_SALT_FALLBACK` is true, its default before 6.1 (`django/core/signing.py:_unsign_cookie`; [What changed in security: Content Security Policy and signing](security.md)).

`EmailBackend.open` now makes a new connection the backend's only once STARTTLS and the login have succeeded (`django/core/mail/backends/smtp.py:EmailBackend.open`; [Sending email: `mailers` and the email backends](../services/mailers.md)).

`GDALRaster.check_raster_lookup_value` refuses a dictionary, a string or a path with `DisallowedRasterLookup`, a `SuspiciousOperation` (`django/contrib/gis/gdal/raster/source.py:GDALRaster.check_raster_lookup_value`).

`BaseSpatialField.get_prep_value` raises it for a dictionary at once, for a string only if it fails as a `GEOSGeometry` and begins "/vsi" or looks like JSON, and never for a `GDALRaster` (`django/contrib/gis/db/models/fields.py:BaseSpatialField.get_prep_value`; [Spatial fields: the geometry fields and `RasterField`](../contrib/spatial-fields.md)).
A `GDALRaster` made from bytes gives its in-memory file exactly their length (`django/contrib/gis/gdal/raster/source.py:GDALRaster.__init__`).
